calls.headline: EGX30 regains 50,700 as Arab and foreign buyers return
calls.body: The EGX30 rose 1.44% to 50,711.96 and the EGX70 EWI 3.41% to 17,098.16 on Monday, on EGP 7.56bn of turnover (Arab Finance), with 196 stocks up and 10 down. Arabs bought a net EGP 52.6m and foreigners EGP 52m while Egyptians sold EGP 104.7m (Youlyou); foreigners and Arabs made up 13.5% of trading. Palm Hills rose 4.7% and Telecom Egypt 2.2%. Volume on the EGX30 was the lowest in a year, and Wall Street's 4.7% jump came after the EGX had closed.
calls.view: A relief bounce on thin volume, not a turn: half of Sunday's 2.85% fall came back, but locals still sold, and Misr Life's offering will draw up to EGP 10.2bn of cash by November 30. Wall Street's rally and cheaper oil help Tuesday's open; a Fed hike priced as certain and the dollar index at 104.32 cap foreign appetite. The desk expects the EGX30 to hold between 48,000 and 53,000 into the IMF board vote. Low confidence.
calls.wrong: The EGX30 closes below 48,000 or above 53,000 before December 15.
calls.notice: The net flows by investor group come from one report (Youlyou); Masrawy gives the same sizes with the signs reversed, so the view does not rely on them.

calls.headline: Misr Life's IPO prices its whole range below fair value
calls.line: The state sells 15% of its life insurer for EGP 9.0–10.2bn, the fifth EGX listing of 2026.
calls.body: Misr Life Insurance opens its books on Tuesday at EGP 12.00–13.60 a share for 750m existing shares, 15% of the company, raising EGP 9.0–10.2bn for Misr Insurance Holding and valuing it at EGP 60–68bn; the whole range sits below adviser BDO's EGP 13.82 fair value (EnterpriseAM, Daily News Egypt). Institutions take 95% and bid until November 27; the public subscribes until November 30, with trading expected around December 3. EnterpriseAM puts the range at 10.4–11.8 times 2025 profit.
calls.view: Priced to sell: a discount to fair value and a state seller that needs the program to work make strong institutional demand likely. The cost falls on the rest of the market: up to EGP 10.2bn must be found within a week, more than the EGP 7.56bn the whole EGX traded on Monday, so small caps and this year's listings may lag until trading starts. Medium confidence.
calls.wrong: The shares are priced at the bottom of the range, or the EGX70 EWI rises more than 5% before November 30.

calls.headline: IMF staff deal steadies the pound as Fed hike bets harden
calls.line: Up to $2.3bn awaits the IMF board before December 15, while futures now price a December Fed hike as certain.
calls.body: The central bank's dollar rate held at EGP 54.30 buy and 54.44 sell on Tuesday morning, from 54.50 on Monday morning (central bank, Youm7). The IMF's staff-level agreement on the final review would release about $1.5bn from the Extended Fund Facility and up to $800m from the Resilience and Sustainability Facility once its board approves (CairoScene, The Rahnuma Daily). Abroad, futures price a December 9 Fed hike as certain, against 89% on Friday, the 10-year Treasury yield rose to 4.94% in Asia and the dollar index closed at 104.32, its highest since March 2025 (Reuters).
calls.view: The IMF money and record remittances outweigh the strong dollar for now: the desk expects the dollar to stay between EGP 53 and 56 into the board vote. The squeeze is on the carry: a Fed hike narrows the gap over 26% bills, so a cut by the central bank on December 17 looks unlikely, which keeps banks' bill income high and developers waiting. Medium confidence.
calls.wrong: The dollar closes above EGP 56 before December 15, or the IMF board delays the review.

calls.headline: Brent slides to $89.37, trimming Egypt's fuel bill
calls.line: Libya's Sharara restart and Trump's signal of talks with Iran took Brent to its lowest settlement since August 28.
calls.body: Brent settled 3.46% lower at $89.37 on Monday and WTI 3.88% lower at $80.17, Brent's lowest since August 28, as Libya reopened its Sharara pipeline and Trump signaled talks with Iran (Nation Thailand, Rigzone/Bloomberg). Iraq is weighing supplying Egypt about 10 million barrels of crude, including routes that avoid Hormuz, with no price or schedule yet (EnterpriseAM, Iraqi News Agency).
calls.view: Cheaper oil cuts the dollars Egypt needs for fuel imports and eases inflation ahead of the December 17 meeting, a quiet support for the pound. Attacks around Hormuz are at their highest since the war began and OPEC+ meets on November 29, so the fall can reverse; the desk expects Brent to stay below $95 through December. Low confidence.

calls.headline: Huang's return lifts Nvidia 31.5% and the Nasdaq 6.5%
calls.body: Nvidia's board reinstated Jensen Huang as chief executive on Monday, 11 days after his ouster, and the stock jumped 31.5% to $165.05, its biggest daily gain since 2003, restoring nearly $1tn of value (Reuters, MLQ.ai). The S&P 500 rose 4.73% to 7,237.17, the Nasdaq 6.51% to 24,089.56 and the Dow 3.01% to 49,595.31, the best day since April 2025; Intel rose 16.3%, Oracle 12.3%, Tesla 11.5% and CoreWeave 22.3%.
calls.view: The rally removes a key-person discount, not the questions behind the rout: Nvidia is still 31% below its October 6 record close of $239.24, and an SEC review of its accounting is open. With a Fed hike now priced as certain, the desk expects the Nasdaq to give back part of Monday's gain before the December 9 decision rather than run to new highs. Low confidence.
calls.wrong: The Nasdaq closes above 25,000 before December 9.

calls.headline: Futures now price a December Fed hike as certain
calls.line: The 10-year yield rose to 4.94% in Asia; October PCE inflation on Wednesday is the last big test.
calls.body: Fed funds futures price a quarter-point hike on December 9 as certain, against 89% on Friday, with about a 5% chance of half a point, and the 10-year Treasury yield rose to 4.94% in Asian trading on Tuesday (Reuters). BlackRock's institute expects one hike in December and another in the first half of 2027. October PCE inflation and the third-quarter GDP estimate come on Wednesday.
calls.view: Monday's rally loosened financial conditions, which is why hike odds rose: good news for stocks is now hawkish. Rate-sensitive groups, housing, small caps and long-duration tech, carry the risk if PCE runs hot. The desk expects the 10-year to stay above 4.70% into the decision. Medium confidence.
calls.wrong: The 10-year yield closes below 4.70% before December 9.

calls.headline: CrowdStrike bids $43.9bn in stock for Zscaler; its shares drop 8.9%
calls.line: 1.135 CrowdStrike shares for each Zscaler share, a 34% premium, in the sector's largest deal.
calls.body: CrowdStrike agreed to buy Zscaler in an all-stock deal worth about $43.9bn at Friday's prices, $260.41 a share and a 34% premium; Zscaler holders would own 15.9% of the combined company (EnterpriseAM, citing the joint statement; Kalkine Media, on CrowdStrike's Form 425 filing). CrowdStrike fell 8.9% to $208.97 on a day the Nasdaq rose 6.5%.
calls.view: The market is charging CrowdStrike for dilution and integration risk at a rich valuation, and with the price set in shares the fall already shrinks Zscaler's premium. The desk expects CrowdStrike to lag software peers until a regulatory timetable is clear. Low confidence.

calls.headline: Meta pauses its $60bn share sale; Oracle says OpenAI build is funded
calls.line: A Delaware trial in April 2027 holds up Meta's Class C stock, while Oracle's funding news lifts it 12.3%.
calls.body: Meta said it will not issue its planned non-voting Class C shares while a Delaware Court of Chancery suit proceeds, with trial set for April 19, 2027, delaying a $60bn at-the-market sale meant to fund AI spending (Meta's 8-K via TradingView; BigGo Finance). Oracle rose 12.3% to $113.68 after saying its roughly $300bn OpenAI contract is fully funded following a $20bn raise (MarketBeat, JKN). Amazon agreed to buy Decart's AI optimization software for about $7.5bn, Bloomberg reported, to support its Trainium chips (GeekWire, TechCrunch).
calls.view: How the AI build-out is paid for now moves these stocks as much as demand does: Meta must lean on debt and cash flow into 2027, and Oracle is still 41.7% down this year after Monday's jump. The desk prefers the spenders that fund from cash to the borrowers. Low confidence.

view.headline: The IMF vote keeps the dollar in EGP 53–56
view.body: The pound held at EGP 54.44 on Tuesday after losing about 1% since Thursday, as US yields near 5% and import and debt payments drew on dollars. The IMF board's vote on the final review, worth up to $2.3bn before December 15, record remittances, Brent at its lowest since August and $3bn of planned international issues should keep the dollar within EGP 53–56; bills at 26.29% keep foreign holders paid to stay even as a Fed hike narrows the gap.
view.wrong: The dollar closes above EGP 56 before December 15, or the IMF board delays the review.
